response.sql:
WITH race_counts AS (
  SELECT r.raceId, c.country, COUNT(cr.constructorResultsId) as entry_count, COALESCE(SUM(cr.points), 0) as total_points
  FROM races r
  JOIN circuits c ON r.circuitId = c.circuitId
  LEFT JOIN constructorResults cr ON r.raceId = cr.raceId
  GROUP BY r.raceId, c.country
),
avg_count AS (
  SELECT AVG(entry_count) as avg_entry_count
  FROM race_counts
)
SELECT rc.raceId, rc.country, rc.total_points, rc.entry_count, rc.entry_count - ac.avg_entry_count as difference
FROM race_counts rc
CROSS JOIN avg_count ac
WHERE rc.entry_count > ac.avg_entry_count
ORDER BY difference DESC
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: LEFT JOIN includes all races from the races table (including those with 0 constructorResults entries) when calculating the average entry count. The phrase "average entry count across all races" refers to all races in the database, not just races with constructorResults records.

alternatives.interpretation: Use INNER JOIN to consider only races that have at least one constructorResults entry. The average is then calculated only across races with entries, and "all races" refers to that filtered set.
